title: Stellarnet GovCloud Listing Readiness & Pilot Huddle
summary: Quick technical huddle to validate Stellarnet's GovCloud marketplace listing requirements, confirm KMS/VPC compatibility, define pilot test harness, and agree next steps for a 4-week readiness pilot. Action items assigned for helm/packaging, telemetry runbook, and a latency/quantization benchmark that matches Stellarnet's 99thpct SLO.
topics: VPC peering and Private deployment networking
Pilot scope: canary, benchmarks, success criteria
Security and compliance artifacts (SOC 2 / audit log visibility)
action_items: Daniel Park (Redwood SE): produce Helm chart diff and packaging checklist, include govcloud-specific values, due 2026-04-23
Sofia Martinez (Stellarnet): share internal pilot dataset, sample traffic shape and peak qps, due 2026-04-19
Maya Chen (AE): send pricing/committed capacity examples and pilot SOW draft, due 2026-04-20
Liam O'Connor (Stellarnet): confirm required KMS/HSM certs and data retention policy doc, due 2026-04-22
Both teams: schedule 60-min pilot kickoff lab to run latency + quantization benchmark, target week of 2026-04-27
next_steps: Redwood to drop playbook and runbook link: https://redwood.app/drive/stellarnet-govcloud-playbook-v1
Set pilot kickoff calendar invite (Maya to propose times)
Redwood SE to provision sandbox govcloud tenant with restricted creds for Stellarnet smoke tests
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got 60 minutes allotted. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me is Daniel our SE. Quick intro?
[00:08] Raj Patel: Raj here, CTO at Stellarnet, joining from DC, thanks for setting this up. Sofia and Liam are with me.
[00:14] Sofia Martinez: hi all, Sofia, platform eng, will own the pilot run.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Liam, security lead. we'll be validating KMS and audit trails.
[00:22] Daniel Park: great, thanks, quick agenda: packaging/listing checklist, govcloud KMS, networking/VPC peering options, pilot scope and benchmarks.
[00:30] Maya: first Q for Stellarnet — what's the non‑negotiable for GovCloud listing? data residency? extra certs?
[00:36] Raj: yes, two things: data cannot leave GovCloud regions for this use case, and we need bring‑your‑own KMS — HSM backed ideally. Also, audit logs must be retained 2 years and accessible for audits.
[00:48] Liam: and we have to show SAML SSO integration with our IdP and RBAC controls.
[00:54] Daniel: okay, that's inline with Redwood Private options. For GovCloud we can offer a private deployment with a customer‑managed VPC + KMS integration. There are a couple of deployment patterns — either full private control plane or a hybrid where control plane is in hosted region but data plane stays in GovCloud.
[01:10] Raj: Hybrid might be easier initially but must ensure the KV cache and logs never traverse public regions. we've seen misconfig in other vendors where traces leaked to centralized analytics.
[01:20] Maya: noted. Daniel, can you explain how our KMS integration works and what certs we need?
[01:26] Daniel: sure. Redwood supports external KMS via standard gRPC wrapper or AWS KMS APIs; for HSM we can integrate through a KMIP compatible gateway. There is a slight gap: some GovCloud HSMs have custom endpoints, need to add endpoint allow‑list in our runtime. We also need to validate key usage policies for signing vs decryption.
[01:44] Liam: are we talking about envelope encryption flows or raw key material? we cannot allow key export.
[01:50] Daniel: envelope encryption only — runtime never sees plaintext keys. We do a local DEK encrypted with customer KEK in KMS. We can add HSM attestation logs to audit trail.
[01:58] Raj: good. next, packaging: what does Redwood require for an App Marketplace listing?
[02:04] Maya: packaging is basically a Helm chart with a small wrapper plus a listing manifest. For GovCloud we recommend a sealed secrets flow and a values file that toggles the region and KMS endpoints. We also provide a packaging checklist that includes image provenance, SBOM, signed container images.
[02:20] Sofia: can you share that checklist? we have a CI process that gates images but want to map to your items.
[02:25] Daniel: yes, we'll share the helm diff. typical items: values.yaml.govcloud, sealer keys, vault integration, network policies (deny by default), init container for node tuning, and a sandbox policy for least privilege.
[02:38] Raj: for the pilot we want to run with 2 model variants: a quantized 8‑bit fastpath and a fp16 variant for quality checks. what do you recommend?
[02:48] Daniel: common pattern is start with FP16 for baseline quality, then iterate quant profiles. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles given sample prompts. For latency SLOs, a 8‑bit q4_0 path can reduce token cost by ~40% and latency by 20% in our benches, but you should validate on your prompt distribution.
[03:06] Sofia: we have bursts up to 180 qps and 99th percentile latency target of 250ms for inference. is that feasible?
[03:14] Daniel: 250ms 99th at 180 qps is aggressive depending on model size and sequence length. For a 13B class model in q8 fastest path on A100 or equivalent we can approach it with optimized kernels and batching, but it may require reserved capacity and a tuned batching profile.
[03:30] Raj: that brings pricing into scope, we likely need dedicated pools. Maya will share examples.
[03:35] Maya: yes, I'll attach committed capacity examples and a sample SOW for a 4‑week pilot.
[03:41] [03:41] Sofia: on telemetry — we need token level cost breakdowns and per‑route latency. do you expose that via console or API?
[03:47] Daniel: both. Redwood Console has per‑route dashboards and a telemetry API to pull raw traces. For GovCloud we can ship telemetry to your internal prometheus + Loki stack via a push gateway or a pull‑only read interface; we don't require sending raw user text.
[04:02] Liam: audit logs — must be immutable and access controlled. do logs ever go to a central hosted analytics by default?
[04:08] Daniel: not by default on Private. For hybrid options there's an opt‑in telemetry aggregator in our hosted plane; for your case we'll ensure logs stay in your bucket and set up cross‑account read only roles for Redwood support if needed.
[04:20] Raj: excellent. can we get a runbook for incident playbooks and rollback?
[04:24] Maya: yes, we'll include runbook templates. usually rollback is automatic to previous model variant or fallback to a lower‑cap model. you can configure canary percent and automatic rollback thresholds.
[04:35] Sofia: about canary: we want 5% traffic for 48 hours then ramp. can your routing logic do weighted routing with automatic evals?
[04:43] Daniel: yes, route by policy and we can tie regressions to prompt set results. if quality drops beyond a threshold for specified prompts we auto rollback. we also support A/B tests and manual gating.
[04:55] [04:55] Raj: are there any known caveats for GovCloud networking? e.g., NATing egress or required endpoints?
[05:02] Daniel: you need to allow egress to our container registry endpoints and any model artifact store endpoints. For GovCloud sometimes those are region isolated — we can host a mirrored artifact repo inside your VPC for the pilot.
[05:14] Liam: mirror would be preferable. also we need to run a pen test, do you have SOC2 artifacts and a penetration test schedule?
[05:22] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II reports and penetration test summaries; we'll share them. the marketplace listing requires at least SOC2 plus a signed attestation.
[05:30] Sofia: timeline question — we want to hit a pilot kickoff in 2 weeks and go 4 weeks. realistic?
[05:35] Maya: yes, assuming we get the helm chart and sample traffic this week. Daniel can provision the sandbox.
[05:41] Daniel: I'll provision a sandbox GovCloud tenant with restricted creds. We'll also set up a small perf harness that replays your sample traffic and captures latency and token cost.
[05:51] Raj: about perf harness — will you run quantization bench too? we want side‑by‑side results for fp16 vs q8_0 vs q4_0.
[05:59] Daniel: yes, bench will test three profiles and produce a CSV with p50/p95/p99, token cost, and memory footprint. We'll also include a trace of KV cache hit rate so you can tune prefix caching.
[06:12] Sofia: what about storage for cached keys / kv cache? needs to be ephemeral and flushed on deploy.
[06:17] Daniel: KV cache is ephemeral in memcached or redis managed inside your VPC — ephemeral by design. we can set eviction policies to flush on rollout.
[06:26] Liam: one more security nit: will support personnel need cross‑account access? if so we need least privilege role and audit trail for those actions.
[06:33] Daniel: yes, support roles can be read‑only and tokenized. every action is logged; we can add a shim to push those logs to your SIEM.
[06:42] Maya: okay, nearing end of time. quick recap of deliverables.
[06:46] Raj: go ahead.
[06:48] Maya: Redwood: share playbook + SOC2 artifact + sample SOW (Maya) by 2026‑04‑20. SE: helm diff and provision sandbox (Daniel) by 2026‑04‑23. Stellarnet: share sample dataset and KMS/HSM certs (Sofia/Liam) by 2026‑04‑22. Pilot kickoff week of 2026‑04‑27.
[07:05] Sofia: thanks, will share dataset and a short traffic matrix.
[07:08] Raj: we'll review SOW and confirm budget.
[07:11] Liam: we'll compile KMS certs and data retention policy.
[07:15] Maya: great. I'll follow up with links and a calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[07:20] [07:20] Meeting ends
